# Setup, Packages and References

:::{.callout-note title="Draft"}
First draft, 2026-10-19. The setup material moved here from the old Welcome chapter.
:::

## R and an Editor

Install R from [www.r-project.org](https://www.r-project.org/). You'll want an editor that knows about R as well. [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) is what most people use, and [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/) is its newer sibling from the same company. Either one runs everything in the book. This build of the book used R version 4.5.2 (2025-10-31).

If you are new to R, [YaRrr! The Pirate's Guide to R](https://bookdown.org/ndphillips/YaRrr/) is a friendly place to start. The book assumes you can read a data frame, call a function and look at its help page, and not much more.

## dplR

`dplR` is on CRAN:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
install.packages("dplR")
```
:::


This build of the book used `dplR` 1.8.1. Check yours with:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
packageVersion("dplR")
```
:::


While the book is being rewritten it runs ahead of CRAN. A few chapters use functions or arguments that are only in the development version, and those chapters will stop with an error on an older `dplR`. The development version lives on GitHub:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("OpenDendro/dplR")
```
:::


Update your packages now and then with `update.packages()`. When a chunk gives you a different answer than it gives me, an old package is the first thing to check.

## Other Packages

Each chapter lists what it loads in its Packages section. You install a package once and then load it with `library` in each session. Here is everything the book uses, read from the file that tells the build server what to install:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pkgs <- read.dcf("DESCRIPTION", fields = "Imports")
pkgs <- trimws(strsplit(pkgs, ",")[[1]])
pkgs
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
 [1] "cowplot"   "dplR"      "forecast"  "gganimate" "ggExtra"   "httr"     
 [7] "knitr"     "magick"    "PNWColors" "rmarkdown" "signal"    "tidyverse"
[13] "waveslim" 
```


:::
:::


To get all of them at once:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
install.packages(setdiff(pkgs, "PNWColors"))
remotes::install_github("jakelawlor/PNWColors")
```
:::


`PNWColors` is a set of color palettes that isn't on CRAN, so it comes from GitHub.
